summary: Full regression after deletion of 10 obsolete modules, unified /our-tasks redirect, designation-based RBAC, HR attendance refactor. Backend: 21/21 tests pass. Frontend: admin flow clean; ops-user sidebar correctly restricted, BUT two RBAC gaps identified at the frontend route level. HR attendance UI ships with all 5 expected data-testids and all 6 cards. Org tree CRUD works. Deleted module endpoints/routes do not 500. No console pageerrors on admin flows.

integration_issues.issue: Ops-user (module_access=['our_tasks','my_profile']) can navigate directly to /hr-admin, /finance, /settings via URL. Backend correctly returns 403 (Network tab shows 403s), but the frontend ProtectedRoute renders the admin UI shell anyway, exposing layout/structure and producing many console errors. Should redirect to /our-tasks (or show 403 page) when target route is outside user.module_access.

Spec says Operations department tabs (Website, Social Media, Meta Ads, SEO, ERP, Finance, HR, Business Dev) should be strictly filtered by designation.operations_departments. Ops-user designation='Operation Head' currently sees ALL department tabs. Either (a) 'Operation Head' designation intentionally has all departments — please confirm in DB, or (b) filter logic is not applied. Recommend verifying designations collection for this designation.

Visiting /sales, /seo, /meta-ads, /bde-tasks does NOT 500 (good) but does NOT 404 or redirect either — SPA renders an empty page with chrome only. Add Navigate redirects for /sales and /seo (existing redirects only cover /seo-board), or a catch-all 404 route. /meta-ads and /bde-tasks DO have explicit Navigate routes (lines 157,159 of App.js) — verify they actually fire.

action_items: Enforce module_access check inside ProtectedRoute so unauthorized users can't render admin pages — currently only backend blocks data via 403.
Verify or add catch-all 404 / Navigate redirects for /sales and /seo (deleted modules render blank shell).
Verify Operations department tab filter actually consults designation.operations_departments — Operation Head sees ALL tabs.
Optional: trim console error spam (403 noise) by gating client fetches on module_access on Ops user.
critical_code_review_comments: ProtectedRoute (frontend) only checks auth, not module_access — route-level RBAC missing.
App.js has no catch-all route — unknown paths render blank SPA shell rather than 404.
GET /api/meetings without trailing slash returns 401 because FastAPI 307 redirect strips Authorization header. Either configure router to allow both, or document; not a regression but a footgun.

success_rate.frontend: ~85% (HR/Org/Operations/Leads/Calendar render correctly; 2 RBAC gaps + deleted-route UX)

seed_data_creation: None. Tests are read-only (org-tree PUT roundtrips current value unchanged).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend regression suite at /app/backend/tests/test_drawlead_regression_jan2026.py covers: auth+RBAC shape (admin vs ops), HR attendance today/summary/employee (cross-user 403 enforced), Org Tree GET+PUT roundtrip, Our Tasks list (both roles) + work-hours/{date} + meetings/, approvals list, leads-v2 list, deleted-module 500 guard for /sales /seo /meta-ads /bde-tasks /sales-tasks. Use trailing slash on /api/meetings/. EmployeeAttendanceViewPage is mounted at /hr-admin/attendance/:userId (NOT /hr-admin/employee-attendance/:userId as review-request doc states — doc mismatch, not bug). HR Page testids confirmed present: attendance-status-tag, attendance-work-mode-tag, work-hours-today, attendance-header-tags, attendance-month-filter. 6 cards visible: Login, Logout, Lunch, Sessions, Login Hour, Work Hours.

rca_of_the_issue.frontend_rbac_gap: ProtectedRoute in /app/frontend/src/components/ProtectedRoute.js likely only verifies auth context — does not consult user.module_access against the current route. Fix: pass required module key in each route element (e.g., <ProtectedRoute module='hr_admin'>) and redirect to /our-tasks if !user.module_access.includes(module).
rca_of_the_issue.deleted_module_blank_pages: App.js Routes has no fallback ('*') route. Add <Route path='*' element={<Navigate to='/our-tasks' replace />} /> as the last route, OR add explicit Navigate entries for legacy /sales and /seo paths (existing redirects only cover /seo-board, /meta-ads, /bde-tasks, /website-projects, etc).
